From: Coordinator, proposed with GC's and Make Distiller Fast's evidence. Approved by the user 2026-11-24 ("proceed", relayed by GC).

Evidence: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-distill-hunt/ctr/mc-report.md, Area 8. A 0x30-byte frame allocation takes 82 instructions on fz, 10 on the BEAM and 11 hand-written.

Scope (narrowed 2026-11-25; GC and Make Distiller Fast agreed the boundary at the Coordinator's request):
- The inline bump sequence only: tip and limit load with one ldp, the tip is computed once, the process pointer is copied once, and the site-table address is built once per function.
- Not here: the captures' run-time kind test (fz-9x7.44.8 removes it), and how the bump's slow path (fz_heap_room) is reached and what stays live across it. That call site belongs to Make Distiller Fast's cold-runtime-call proposal, which applies one rule to every rarely taken runtime call.

Findings for the bump (survey on 807cf8e1d): the process pointer is copied twice by our IR (process_arg caches get_pinned_reg per block, fn_ctx.rs:101-109; emit_place spans 3 blocks); the tip is computed twice by Cranelift rematerialising new_top in the inline block (hypothesis: pass it as a block parameter); ldp fusion and the per-function site-table address are checked by disassembly.

Done when: the frame allocation's disassembly matches the hand-written bump; distiller instructions measured before and after; no pin rises.

comments.text: From: GC. Investigation done (survey on 807cf8e1d): the captures' kind test is CaptureStores::store_open_ref_word (closure.rs, StoredRefKind::Open), the slot-naming scalar ref of kinds 0xA..=0xE; fz-9x7.44.8 removes it (capture store becomes str + strb) and .44.8 cannot land partly, so it leaves this ticket. Remaining scope is the bump only: process pointer copied twice comes from our IR (process_arg caches get_pinned_reg per block, fn_ctx.rs:101-109; emit_place spans 3 blocks); tip computed twice is Cranelift rematerialising new_top in the inline block (hypothesis: pass it as a block param); ldp fusion and the site-table address once per function are unverified and checked by disassembly.

title: The inline bump is the hand-written sequence
